Informed Consent Form for Participants Earning Credits Online

IRB-FY2021-4944

Introduction

You are invited to take part in a research study named Language comprehension: brain and behavioral mechanisms. The study is designed to learn more about how the brain processes language. The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: be interviewed about your handedness, and make judgments and responses to different types of auditory and visual stimuli, which may include sinusoidal or “pure” tones, noise, flashes, voices, speech and written words. Video/audio recordings may be taken to confirm that the tasks are performed correctly. You will be notified if these recordings will be taken. All personal identifying information will be removed from such recordings: the camera will be focused on your lips and hand(s), and these recordings will be assigned random codes for each participant for purposes of confidentiality.

Compensation

Your participation will take about 1 hour, and you will receive 1 credit. If you are taking part in a multi-session study, you will be asked to return for a series of experiments and the credit assignment will be delayed until you complete all agreed-to sessions. If you choose to leave the study short of the number of requested sessions, you will be granted a number of credits relative to the number of completed hours. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive partial credits. If you are a member of Prof. Poeppel’s lab, you will not receive any credits.

Risks and benefits

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. Although you will receive no direct benefits for participation in this study, it may make you more aware of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how the human brain interprets language.

Confidentiality

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. The code key connecting your name to specific information about you will be kept in a separate, secure location. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes. However, your name or other identifiers, such as voice or pictures that could identify you, will not be used in any publication or teaching materials without your specific permission, which will be requested in writing. You can request to review any photographic, audio, or video recordings of your experimental sessions and request that all or any portion of the recordings be destroyed. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers, NYU or non-NYU affiliated, without additional consent. No information that identifies you by name will be released without separate consent except as required by law. 

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns.

The Poeppel lab is committed to facilitating transparency and collaboration within the research community wherever possible. In accordance with the recommendations of the American Psychological Association, we will maintain study data for at least 5 years following publication in order to allow for potential replication and/or follow-up studies. Hard copy records of your data will be securely digitized and the physical copies will be destroyed. All electronic records will be stored on a secure drive located in the principal investigator's office.

We ask your permission to share your anonymized data as outlined above. If you choose not to allow your anonymized data to be shared, you will not be able to participate in this study. Please understand that giving your permission for anonymized data sharing is only for the purpose of helping us contribute to open source research; it does not mean that your data will be any less secure or that confidentiality of identifiable data will be compromised in any way. Please check the box and sign below:

I authorize the principal investigator, David Poeppel, and his co-investigators to share the results of this experiment, including demographics, behavioral, physiological, neuropsychological, and neuroimaging data with other researchers, both NYU and non-NYU affiliated; I understand that all my research records will be anonymized.

Rights

If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study. Taking part in this study is voluntary. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough verbal and written explanation of it will be provided. 

If there is anything about the study or your participation that is unclear or that you do not understand, if you have questions or wish to report a research-related problem, you may contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003. For questions about your rights as a research participant, you may contact the University Committee on Activities Involving Human Subjects, New York University, 665 Broadway, Suite 804, New York, New York, 10012, at ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu or (212) 998-4808. 

You may request a copy of this consent document to keep or have it emailed to you.

PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

Introduction

You are invited to take part in a research study named Language comprehension: brain and behavioral mechanisms. The study is designed to learn more about how the brain processes language. Video/audio recordings may be taken to confirm that the tasks are performed correctly. You will be notified if these recordings will be taken. All personal identifying information will be removed from such recordings: the camera will be focused on your lips and hand(s), and these recordings will be assigned random codes for each participant for purposes of confidentiality.

If you choose to leave the study short of the number of requested sessions, you will be granted a number of credits relative to the number of completed hours. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive partial credits. If you are a member of Prof. Poeppel’s lab, you will not receive any credits.

The code key connecting your name to specific information about you will be kept in a separate, secure location. You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY

Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. RESEARCH INFORMED CONSENT FORM FOR DEPARTMENT POOL PARTICIPANTS EARNING CREDIT IRB-FY2025-9903

STUDY TITLE: Narrative Comprehension IRB-FY2025-9903


INVESTIGATOR(S): David Poeppel, Hanzhi Chen


INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.


AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE 

By continuing with this study, you agree to participate. Make sure you understand what the study involves before you agree. If you have questions about the study after you agree to participate, you should contact the research team. Do you wish to participate in the study?

INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.


AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE 

By continuing with this study, you agree to participate. Make sure you understand what the study involves before you agree. If you have questions about the study after you agree to participate, you should contact the research team. Do you wish to participate in the study?

Thank you for participating in our study. You will listen to two audio stories and then answer questions about their details to evaluate your comprehension. We ask that you pay attention to the stories and corresponding questions as we hope you will attempt to maximize your score overall.

INVESTIGATOR(S): David Poeppel, Hanzhi Chen


INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.


AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE

PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. Video/audio recordings may be taken to confirm that the tasks are performed correctly. You will be notified if these recordings will be taken. All personal identifying information will be removed from such recordings: the camera will be focused on your lips and hand(s), and these recordings will be assigned random codes for each participant for purposes of confidentiality.

Compensation

Your participation will take about 1 hour, and you will receive 1 credit. If you are taking part in a multi-session study, you will be asked to return for a series of experiments and the credit assignment will be delayed until you complete all agreed-to sessions. If you choose to leave the study short of the number of requested sessions, you will be granted a number of credits relative to the number of completed hours. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive partial credits. If you are a member of Prof. Poeppel’s lab, you will not receive any credits.

Risks and benefits

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. Although you will receive no direct benefits for participation in this study, it may make you more aware of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how the human brain interprets language.

Confidentiality

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. The code key connecting your name to specific information about you will be kept in a separate, secure location. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes. However, your name or other identifiers, such as voice or pictures that could identify you, will not be used in any publication or teaching materials without your specific permission, which will be requested in writing. You can request to review any photographic, audio, or video recordings of your experimental sessions and request that all or any portion of the recordings be destroyed. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers, NYU or non-NYU affiliated, without additional consent. No information that identifies you by name will be released without separate consent except as required by law. 

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns.

The Poeppel lab is committed to facilitating transparency and collaboration within the research community wherever possible. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough verbal and written explanation of it will be provided. 

If there is anything about the study or your participation that is unclear or that you do not understand, if you have questions or wish to report a research-related problem, you may contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003. The code key connecting your name to specific information about you will be kept in a separate, secure location. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers, NYU or non-NYU affiliated, without additional consent. No information that identifies you by name will be released without separate consent except as required by law.

Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers, NYU or non-NYU affiliated, without additional consent. RESEARCH INFORMED CONSENT FORM FOR DEPARTMENT POOL PARTICIPANTS EARNING CREDIT IRB-FY2025-9903

STUDY TITLE: Narrative Comprehension IRB-FY2025-9903


INVESTIGATOR(S): David Poeppel, Hanzhi Chen


INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.


AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE 

By continuing with this study, you agree to participate. Make sure you understand what the study involves before you agree. If you have questions about the study after you agree to participate, you should contact the research team. Do you wish to participate in the study?

INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.

INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.

Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study.

INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.

RESEARCH INFORMED CONSENT FORM FOR DEPARTMENT POOL PARTICIPANTS EARNING CREDIT IRB-FY2025-9903

STUDY TITLE: Narrative Comprehension IRB-FY2025-9903


INVESTIGATOR(S): David Poeppel, Hanzhi Chen


INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.


AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE 

By continuing with this study, you agree to participate. Make sure you understand what the study involves before you agree. If you have questions about the study after you agree to participate, you should contact the research team. Do you wish to participate in the study?

INVITATION TO BE A PART OF A RESEARCH STUDY:

You are invited to participate in a research study. This form has information to help you decide whether or not you wish to participate—please review it carefully. Your participation is voluntary. Please ask any questions you have about the study or about this form before deciding to participate.  


PURPOSE OF THE STUDY

The study is designed to learn more about how humans process and memorize narratives. In this study, we wanted to learn more about how people remember stories and decide whether certain details about them are true or false. Sometimes, when we remember things, we might recall them differently from what actually happened. We were interested in seeing how people agree or disagree on what they remember after hearing a story. 


DESCRIPTION OF STUDY PROCEDURES

If you agree to participate, you will be asked to listen to spoken stories. You will listen to a random set of two stories out of 4 existing options. After each story, you will see different statements about the story and decide whether you agreed with them or not, or sometimes multiple choice questions about details of the story. These statements were designed to test how well you remembered the story and whether your memory matched what other people remembered. The stories are each 8-13 minutes, and the questions should take 10-20 minutes for each story.

The research is being conducted by Prof. David Poeppel, Ph.D., who is the Principal Investigator, as part of his faculty research in the NYU Department of Psychology. If you agree to be in this study, you will be asked to: listen to auditory narratives that have been publicly recorded, make judgments to questions related to the content of the narratives.

RISKS OR DISCOMFORTS

There are no known risks associated with your participation in this research beyond those of everyday life. The data collected has the risk of a breach of confidentiality as they contain code associated in the SONA system with personal information.

BENEFITS

It is hoped that this study will contribute to your understanding of how knowledge is discovered in psychology and help the investigator better understand how memory of different events in a story is reflected in recall.

COMPENSATION

You will receive 1 credit. If you withdraw before the end of the study, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. If you choose not to participate, you can fulfill the course requirement in other ways besides participating in this study.

VOLUNTARY PARTICIPATION

Participating in this study is completely voluntary. You may choose not to take part in the study or to stop participating at any time, for any reason, without penalty or negative consequences. Not taking part or withdrawing from the study will not affect your grade or academic standing in any way. You have the right to skip or not answer any questions you prefer not to answer. When you complete the study, a thorough explanation of it will be provided.


If you withdraw from the study early but have already started on the survey questions, you will receive credit for the time you have completed. You should email the researcher with the number of questions you’ve completed.


If you withdraw or are withdrawn from the study early, then we will not keep information about you that is already collected.

PRIVACY & DATA CONFIDENTIALITY 

In this study, you may be asked to provide information that could be used to identify you personally. This information will be kept confidential. Only researchers and others that will keep the information confidential (e.g., regulatory agencies or oversight groups) may access information that could personally identify you. 

Confidentiality of your research records will be strictly maintained by assigning random code numbers to each participant and reporting all data in coded form. Your associated SONA ID will be kept in a secure location (NYU Box drive) separate from the data analysis. Your SONA ID is personally identifiable information as they can be connected to your name and email in the NYU SONA system. Information not containing identifiers may be used in future research or shared with other researchers without additional consent. The results of any portion of this study may be published in a book or journal or used for teaching purposes.

Information about you collected for this study may be shared with other researchers, used for other research studies, or placed in a data repository. These studies may be similar to this study or completely different. All information that could identify you will be removed before sharing the data or using it for other research studies. We will not ask you for additional permission before sharing the information.

The researcher cannot keep information confidential if they have concerns that someone is hurting children, that someone is hurting you, or that you might hurt yourself or someone else. In such cases, they will inform people in authority about their concerns. 

ACCESS TO YOUR STUDY INFORMATION 

We will not give you access to the information that is collected about you in this study. 


CONTACT INFORMATION

You are encouraged to ask questions at any time during this study. For information about the study, contact David Poeppel at (212) 992 7489 or david.poeppel@nyu.edu, 6 Washington Place, New York, NY 10003.  


If you have questions about your rights as a research participant or if you believe you have been harmed from the research, please contact the NYU Human Research Protection Program at (212)998-4808 or ask.humansubjects@nyu.edu.


AGREEMENT TO PARTICIPATE 

By continuing with this study, you agree to participate. Make sure you understand what the study involves before you agree. If you have questions about the study after you agree to participate, you should contact the research team. Do you wish to participate in the study?

Thank you for participating in our study. You will listen to two audio stories and then answer questions about their details to evaluate your comprehension. We ask that you pay attention to the stories and corresponding questions as we hope you will attempt to maximize your score overall.
